A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Table-Critic. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-E are readable and support a reliable comparison, including the additional Curator documentation in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original WikiTQ and TabFact experiments, including benchmark comparisons, refinement analyses, computational costs and a template-evolution ablation.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The four agents, refinement loop and template-tree operations remain unchanged. Algorithm 2 and the new Curator prompts document the existing template addition and vertical/horizontal expansion mechanisms described in v1 Section 3.4.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate WikiTQ table question answering and TabFact fact verification. No dataset, domain or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains End-to-End QA, Few-Shot QA, Binder, Dater, Chain-of-Table and Critic-CoT. The critic comparisons in Table 2 and the Chain-of-Table self-consistency comparison in Figure 3 also retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: Both retain 4,344 WikiTQ and 2,024 TabFact test samples, the same three backbone models, five default refinement iterations and temperature 0.0. The iteration analysis, self-consistency settings and evaluation metrics are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The critic-effectiveness, iteration, computational-cost and static-template analyses remain unchanged, as do the existing table-reasoning examples. Figures 10-13 provide Curator instructions and schematic outputs with placeholders, without adding an empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The existing point-estimate reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in Tables 1-4, plotted results in Figures 2-3 and corresponding findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains Table-Critic's average accuracies of 73.7% on WikiTQ and 91.7% on TabFact.

T1.justification: The formal agent descriptions and computational-cost definitions and derivations in Equations 1-6 are unchanged. The added Curator pseudocode supplies implementation documentation without new mathematical results, assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about the four-agent framework, iterative refinement, evolving template tree and advantages in accuracy, error correction, stability and efficiency.

C2.justification: The interpretations of task differences, convergence, correction stability and computational costs are unchanged. The Limitations section retains the textual-table focus and potential multimodal extensions; the added Curator explanation elaborates the existing mechanism.

D1.justification: Appendix E now documents the Curator's routing and similarity decisions through Algorithm 2 and prompts/example formats in Figures 10-13. The abstract adds a code-repository link. These supplement the existing implementation, serving and decoding details.

R1.justification: v2 adds Xu et al. (2025), Rapsm, to the introduction and bibliography. The research positioning in Section 2 and Appendix A is unchanged; the C-3PO preprint-to-conference update refers to the same work.

P1.justification: Appendix E expands its explanation from three agents to all four, adding Curator paragraphs and cross-references. An Acknowledgments section is added, while the main narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Algorithm 2 and four boxed Curator instruction/example figures, Figures 10-13, and reflows existing appendix figures. The existing experimental tables, plots and framework illustration retain their displays.

improvement.justification: v1 describes Curator operations but omits its prompts from Appendix E. v2 adds decision pseudocode, prompts and example formats, plus a code-access link, improving clarity and reproducibility information for this component. The gain is limited: the new examples contain placeholders, and the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
